detail: auditctl rebuild --dry-run over /projects/dev/_artifacts/agentops/audit/*.ndjson validated 7 shards / 468 events and reported no problem. The sqlite index holds 493. The 25-event difference is entirely workflow.session events published by claude-hook on 2026-08-26: they reached the derived index but never reached the authoritative shard. Two defects: the claude-hook publisher writes the index without appending to the shard, inverting the plan's rule that repo-local shards are authoritative; and rebuild does not detect or report the gap, so the D3 gate would pass while silently dropping 25 events.

detail: The earlier receipt attributed the 25 index-only events to claude-hook writing the index without appending to the shard. Reading auditctl/cli.py add shows the opposite ordering: insert, append, rollback-on-append-failure, then commit. All 25 ids are present in .auditctl/archive/auditctl-retired-2026-08-26.db (488 rows, max ts 2026-08-26T19:04:08Z), so they entered the current index through that day's ledger retirement without their shard lines. The D3 finding itself stands unchanged and is now fixed: rebuild refuses instead of reporting success.

detail: A repo with no .sprintctl/backend.json and no .envrc resolves backend=local from cwd and writes to ~/.sprintctl/sprintctl.db without warning. Four items and a sprint were created there while appearing to succeed. This is the isolation question the plan raises about #1245 from the other side: the failure mode is not a caller reaching another repo scope, it is a participating repo silently leaving the authority altogether. Filed as cred-broker #2323.

detail: Rollout required an unplanned identity-registry migration: vuoro-service 0.1.54 is the first deployed image to require principal_id on every identity, a change merged to vuoro main on 2026-08-22 and never released until today. All four identities minted as vuoro-static:<actor>:0 and validated against the service's own load_identities() before re-encryption; identity-revision 7 -> 8 to force the roll. First attempt (appservice 5bbfe68a) crash-looped on CompositionError with the old pod still serving; second attempt (2ffa40b2) rolled cleanly. next-work and next-work --explain now return ready items in every scope tested.
